failures.test_name: AC-14: compile + test pass — Letflow.Obs.Alerts module exists and exports run_detection/2
failures.root_cause: Missing Code.ensure_loaded!/1 before function_exported?/3. BEAM lazy-loads modules on first runtime reference. When ExUnit's random seed puts AC-14 first (before any test that calls Alerts.run_detection/2), the Letflow.Obs.Alerts module has not yet been loaded and function_exported? returns false. The companion test in the same describe block (for Letflow.Dlq.count_entries/1) already calls Code.ensure_loaded! — the same pattern was not applied to the Alerts test.

notes.suite_runtime: 1415 seconds (~23.6 minutes) — well above typical. Root cause: test/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures_test.exs calls System.cmd(gh.bat) for ~195 tracked issues; on Windows each cmd.exe spawn takes several seconds (Windows Defender scanning newly-created executables in the temp fixture directory). This is a pre-existing Windows performance characteristic, not introduced by REQ-201.
notes.first_run_hung: First mix test run was killed after 38 minutes. The BEAM process entered a zero-CPU state after the output buffer filled (pipe-buffered stdout on Windows) and the audit_issue_closures_test was consuming all wall-clock time spawning subprocesses. On the second run, stdout was redirected directly to a file (> file) rather than through Tee-Object, which produced a larger, growing output file confirming the test was making progress. The process exited normally at +18.5 minutes into the second run.
notes.pre_existing_failures_on_main: The two grep-not-found failures (sandbox_test, host_api_test) are known Windows-only issues present on main before this branch. They are not newly introduced.
